correctness.rationale: For reflexive row-or-column incidence on W=[m]×[n], m,n>=2, the Galois closure of S is intersection of all row-column crosses C_(i,j) containing S (empty intersection=W). Pairwise distinct-cross intersections are entire rows, columns or diagonal two-point sets. Intersecting further yields only singleton or empty, giving exactly ∅,W,mn points,m+n full rows/columns,mn crosses and 2*C(m,2)*C(n,2) diagonal pairs; count 2+2mn+m+n+2*C(m,2)*C(n,2), including degeneracies for m=n=2. At m,n>=3 the join incidence among singleton atoms recovers rook adjacency; automorphisms therefore are independent coordinate permutations and a coordinate swap only for square boards. If one side has 2 rows, closure factorizes into product of two height-2 M_b lattices, allowing S_b wr S2; at 2×2 the product is Boolean on four atoms with group S4. For direct Horn width, every S admits subset T of <=4 points with c(T)=c(S); four corners of a 2×2 subboard need four premises to infer a cell outside their two rows and columns when m,n>=3. Iteratively, pair rules complete any occupied row/column and triple matching forces all W; saturated proper sets are exactly listed closed extents. A three-point transversal with closed pair subsets shows width >=3. Thus direct/iterative widths are (4,3) thick, (2,2) thin non-2×2, (0,0) 2×2. Independent enumeration computed 16,25,44,69 closed sets at 2×2,2×3,3×3,3×4 and matches formula. The finite tests are not used as universal proof.
